wins.text: Firm reported Q4 net income of $14B, EPS of $4.81 on revenue of $43.7B, ROTCE of 21%; full-year net income of $54B, EPS of $18.22, revenue of $173B, ROTCE of 20%
CIB IB fees up 49% YoY with #1 wallet share of 9.3% for 2024; advisory up 41%, debt underwriting up 56%, equity underwriting up 54%
Markets total revenue of $7B, up 21% YoY; Fixed Income up 20%, Equities up 22% on elevated client activity
AWM AUM reached $4 trillion and client assets $5.9 trillion, both up 18% YoY; record long-term net inflows of $234B for full year 2024
CET1 ratio of 15.7%, up 40 bps QoQ; $4B of net common share repurchases in Q4; management signaled intent to arrest excess capital growth via increased buybacks

risks.text: 2025 NII ex Markets guided to ~$90B, implying a YoY decline from 2024 levels, with NII trough expected mid-year driven by rate cuts and deposit margin compression
CCB Banking & Wealth Management revenue down 7% YoY on deposit margin compression and lower deposits; NII ex Markets down $548M or 2% YoY in Q4
Card net charge-offs up $428M YoY to $2.1B; net reserve build of $557M driven by higher revolving balances; 2025 Card NCO rate guided at ~3.6%

Loan growth not materializing despite improved business sentiment post-election; wholesale and commercial loans down 1-2% QoQ; management cited wide-open capital markets and residual policy uncertainty as headwinds

2025 expenses guided to ~$95B, up meaningfully YoY, driven by volume/revenue-related costs, tech investment, marketing, and inflation; management flagged tension between investment spend and efficiency

guidance_items.detail: 2025 NII ex Markets expected ~$90B; firm-wide NII ~$94B including ~$4B Markets NII; NII trough expected mid-year with sequential growth in H2 2025
Card loan growth expected healthy but below 2024's 12% pace as revolver normalization tailwinds are largely behind
2025 Card net charge-off rate guided at ~3.6%, in line with previous guidance
2025 expenses guided to ~$95B, up from 2024 levels, driven by volume/revenue-related costs, tech, marketing, and inflation
Deposit growth expected to stabilize with more visible growth trend in H2 2025; modest deposit margin compression expected due to lower rates

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: CEO succession timeline and identity of successor
G-SIB surcharge bucket risk and stress capital buffer trajectory under evolving regulatory framework
Potential for special dividend as a capital return mechanism
